## 9. Fixed ordinary decoder and the exact reusable error span
Every killed output has r<=U/h<=e_cut N/h, deterministically. Its canonical DATA representative therefore has physical Pauli weight at most alpha N, alpha=e_cut/h. Choose the constants with 2alpha below relative distance, as already allowed by the basin margins.

Fix an ordinary minimum-weight syndrome recovery once, resolving ties independently of time, noise, program labels and target logical gates. If P,Q are two Pauli errors of weight <=alpha N, different syndromes are orthogonal; equal syndromes give a zero-syndrome P dagger Q of weight <d, hence a stabilizer. Recovery acts as a scalar multiple of logical identity on each P Enc(rho)Q dagger term. Linearity handles the ENTIRE coherent span with arbitrary controller/bath coefficients and all reference operators. There is no Pauli-count inflation or stochastic-Pauli-mixture claim.

The fixed syndrome recovery need not equal the component decoder on high-weight states; the global killed span never enters those states. For multiple blocks use the same ordinary product DATA decoder with code-distance constants expressed consistently in the combined N convention. The native forest inverse is still an explicit ideal output operation.

This supplies the exact source-weight input for the separately specified FIXED_PRODUCT_DECODER_SPAN endpoint. On the present killed basin its memory weight-tail term can even be zero by choosing alpha=e_cut/h. After the actual transversal gate, each suffix Pauli coefficient has final weight at most 2(alpha+r_gate beta)N when at most beta N clocks are unfinished; the already reviewed clock inclusion bound gives an exponential aggregate tail for that event. This observation does not insert U_L into the DATA decoder and does not use a prefix-basin or animal-connector argument. A complete programmed-gate statement must still retain its actual onsite gauge, physical program noise, latency and fixed TARGET native forest inverse; those are separate declared interfaces, not consequences of a scalar memory moment alone.

## 10. Warm starts: what is and is not earned
The scalar law (4.2) holds for every positive P-supported initial state. Exponentially protected warm operation requires an EARNED initialization/preparation with the intended canonical logical action and a uniform

    log x(0)<=nu_w N+O(1),
    max(nu_w,nu)+q_t<s'e_cut

by a FIXED positive coefficient gap. It then gives the same exponentially small boundary estimate from time zero. The extensive coefficient contracts toward nu at rate lambda/s; reaching any larger fixed coefficient takes a time independent of N, though perhaps enormous in physical units.

A moment lying only O(1) below the extensive barrier does not imply an exponential tail. A small moment without P-support does not establish the radius condition or basin entry. Later contraction of a killed state cannot retrospectively pay for exits during a high-energy burn-in. Any initially outside-P mass or preparatory channel error must be bounded separately and added contractively. Nor can low syndrome energy certify that the desired logical information was not already replaced by a logical Pauli.

For the standard diamond-channel statement retain the specified fixed logical-independent auxiliary/bath initialization, or an independently earned warm channel with the appropriate logical action and uniform moment. The scalar result is not a claim about arbitrary initial logical/bath assignments. A more general statewise marginal statement can be formulated for a state already in the canonical subsystem: I_L tensor a CP/TNI auxiliary map can be completed by a failure channel, and its missing logical/reference marginal is positive with trace equal to the survival loss. This does not prepare the canonical subsystem, preserve the dynamical bath as an untouched reference, or supply a universal channel assignment for arbitrary correlated inputs.
